items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: the American Theater would bring in French dancers, Celestine and Constance and things like that

ctx.x: What about the audience now? It wouldn't be all French, certainly.

No, it was, again, amusements were limited. However, after the American Theater opened, even the one on Camp Street and then later the St. Charles, there was a great tendency for the French to go to their side and the Americans to go to their side. But both theaters, this is true more often than the American Theater, tried to bring in attractions that would draw the patrons away from the other theater. Thus the American Theater would bring in French dancers, Celestine and Constance and things like that, hoping to…
What about Negroes? Did they have the free Negroes there or slaves?
